purpose: Folded arms clear of bike, closed mouth and tougher expression, continuous handlebar with two outer grips and controls.
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied low-angle El Unicornio motorcycle mock-up. The user requests THREE specific corrections: the unicorn's hands completely OFF the motorcycle, preferably ARMS FOLDED; a CLOSED MOUTH and TOUGH expression; and anatomically/mechanically CORRECT MOTORCYCLE HANDLEBARS with TWO outer-end grips rather than the inaccurate one-sided central grip in the source.

KEEP: the same dramatic LOW CLOSE THREE-QUARTER portrait camera, large round golden headlight in the lower-left foreground, front forks descending beyond the bottom, the unicorn sitting astride the bike rising behind toward the upper-right, desert highway and distant red mesas, blue sky, warm gold lighting, full horn within frame, saturated angular faceted illustrated style. Keep the pink humanoid unicorn identity, lavender muzzle, single pearlescent horn, upright pink ears, black sunglasses, black open-face helmet with chrome trim and horn port, small pastel rainbow mane, black leather jacket, pale aqua turtleneck with sage rolled collar and small unicorn emblem, and butter-yellow pants.

CHARACTER POSE CHANGE: Remove the old left hand from the handlebar completely, remove the old right hand from his thigh, and redraw BOTH arms FOLDED naturally across his chest. A convincing classic crossed-arms pose: two leather-covered forearms across the upper chest with one pink hand resting on the opposite upper arm and the other pink hand partially tucked under the other upper arm. Two shoulders, two elbows, two forearms, exactly two pink hands, no extra limbs, no fingers attached to handlebars. Keep the elbows and hands readable and within the canvas. The arms must sit wholly with the character BEHIND the nearer motorcycle assembly, leaving a clean depth break and no character-to-bike contact at the handlebars. The turtleneck collar must remain clearly visible above folded arms; it is okay if the chest emblem is partly obscured by the natural arm pose. Casual settled seated posture as if stopped for a tough biker portrait, not actively steering.

EXPRESSION CHANGE: CLOSE THE MOUTH completely. No open grin, no teeth, no tongue. Give the long equine face a firm closed neutral mouth line, chin slightly lifted, head turned toward the camera, calm tough self-assured attitude behind sunglasses. Keep him recognizably pink and unicorn-like; do not turn him into a monster, angry caricature, human face or change the muzzle shape. The contrast between pastel unicorn/turtleneck and tough biker pose provides the humor.

HANDLEBAR CORRECTION, CRITICAL: Replace the inaccurate source cockpit/handlebar geometry with ONE physically coherent conventional motorcycle handlebar assembly, clamped at its CENTER above the fork crown with a matched pair of risers, extending continuously out to TWO DISTINCT OUTER ENDS. At EACH OUTERMOST END there is a black rubber handgrip, a small switch/control housing immediately INBOARD of that grip, and a matching metal clutch or brake lever sweeping forward from its mount beside that grip. The grips are at the extreme ends, NOT near the central stem or headlight and NOT in the middle of the bar. The near-side grip appears larger through natural low three-quarter perspective and the far-side grip appears smaller but must remain clearly visible and recognizable as the second handle. Ensure both complete handle ends fit within the image by using modest bar width/sweep and suitable perspective; do not simply cut one handle out of frame. The bar and grips form one credible connected steering system from central mount to both sides. No third grip, no disembodied grip, no extra fork tubes, no oversized floating control box. Remove the current erroneous large protruding black/red box at upper-left and rebuild appropriately sized control housings next to the proper outer grips. Brake/clutch cables can curve neatly toward the central fork assembly without messy tangles. Keep the big headlight and amber turn indicators as the main close foreground feature, with the corrected handlebars visibly above it and below the unicorn's folded arms.

Preserve the scene's perspective and general composition rather than returning to the symmetric front-view mock-up. A small natural amount of additional breathing space is acceptable ONLY if needed to make both complete handlebars and crossed arms legible, but maintain the close upper-body shot and oversized headlight. No full motorcycle or full wheels. Retain sharp warm facets, rich chrome reflections, deep leather shadows and vivid desert color. Single full-bleed portrait composite, approximately 1024 x 1536, no text, border, labels or watermark.
